identity.kind: flat-screen TV (LG Flatron claimed by seller)

claims.claim: This is a scrap LG Flatron TV.
claims.evidence: Brand/model text is not readable in photo 0; only a generic TV appearance is visible.
Photo 0 shows a blank screen with a spinner/loading icon, but it does not prove the TV is faulty (could be input/menu/loading).

claims.evidence: Seller text only; photo 0 does not show internal parts or recycling condition.
Seller text only; no pickup details shown in photo 0.

risks.risk: The TV may not be fully dead; it could be stuck on a menu/input or needs a power/remote/AV selection—so pricing as scrap could be too low/high depending on actual fault.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video showing: power on from cold, selecting inputs (AV/HDMI), and confirming whether there is any picture/audio after troubleshooting.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst case: treat as non-working/for parts only.

risks.risk: Brand/model and screen size are unclear; wrong identity leads to wrong scrap/parts valuation.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the label/sticker on the back showing brand, model number, and screen size.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst case for an older unknown-size flat TV (parts/recycling value).

risks.risk: Physical condition (cracks, panel damage, stand damage) is not fully shown; damage can change parts value.
risks.proof: Ask for photos of the full front, both sides, and the back/stand, plus close-ups of any cracks or dents.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming possible cosmetic/structural wear consistent with scrap.

risks.risk: Accessories/remote/power cable availability affects usability for parts testing and resale.
risks.proof: Ask what comes with it (remote, power cable, stand) and request photos of included items.

proof_requests: Clear back-label photo showing LG/Flatron model number and screen size.
Short video: power on from cold, show input switching (AV/HDMI) and whether any picture/audio appears.
Full-condition photos: front (straight-on), both sides, back, and stand/base close-up.
Confirm what accessories are included (remote, power cable, any adapters).
response.reason: The photo shows a TV with a spinner/loading icon but does not conclusively prove it is non-working, and the brand/model is not readable—so a worst-case scrap price needs proof first.
